interface.title: Monadology Explorer
interface.field: Philosophy / digital humanities (Leibniz's Monadology, Latta translation)
interface.stage_of_work: close reading and exploratory analysis of a curated concept–paragraph knowledge graph
interface.what_it_is_for: A reader picks an editorial theme, starts from a few curated concepts, and reveals the concept–paragraph graph one hop at a time while reading each paragraph's canonical text. A Full graph view shows the whole curated network and its metrics.

data.note: The curated graph ships with the app: 154 nodes (64 concepts, 90 paragraphs) and 292 relationships, one connected component. It includes Latta-translation text for each paragraph and six editorial themes (The Nature of Monads; Natural and Psychic Hierarchy; Truth, Reason, and God; Creation and Harmony; Bodies, Souls, and Nature; Conclusion). Nothing was uploaded.

features.name: Progressive one-hop network reveal with discovery counters
features.general: Start from a few seed items in a network, select one, and expand only its direct neighbours, one step at a time. Everything found stays visible, and counters show how much of the whole network has been uncovered.
features.specific: Pick a theme to load 4 seed concepts, then select a node (Jump to a discovered node, search, or paragraph navigation). Press Reveal connected nodes; the Discovery cards update (Nodes x/154, Paragraphs x/90, Concepts x/64). Reset exploration returns to the seeds.
steps: choose a theme to load its seed concepts
select a visible node from the 'Jump to a discovered node' list
press Reveal connected nodes to add its one-hop neighbours
select one of the new nodes and reveal again for the next hop
watch the Nodes / Paragraphs / Concepts counters
press Reset exploration to start over
serves_tasks: Choose a thematic region to start from and see its seed items
Pick an item that is already visible and inspect its direct relationships
Expand the visible network by exactly one hop from the selected item, keeping everything found so far

features.name: Node detail panel with typed relationship table
features.general: When an item is selected, show its identity, its links listed by type, and a button to expand from it. Its links are highlighted in the network drawing.
features.specific: The Reading & relationships panel shows the node title and type ('Curated philosophical concept') and the Reveal connected nodes button. A Direct relationships table lists Node / Relationship (related to, contrasts with, discusses, develops). The selected node's edges turn red in the graph.
steps: select a node
read its title and type
scan the Direct relationships table by relation type
see its edges highlighted in the graph
press Reveal connected nodes
serves_tasks: Pick an item that is already visible and inspect its direct relationships
Read the source passage for a selected item and see which concepts it is linked to

features.name: Search-to-reveal for concepts or numbered passages
features.general: Type a name or a section number in any common form, choose from the matching items, and add the chosen one to the network as the selected item. A clear message appears when nothing matches.
features.specific: In 'Concept or paragraph', typing a concept name, '§23' or '53' fills a Result dropdown (e.g. 'Harmony · harmony', 'Pre-established Harmony · pre_established_harmony', '§53 · p053'). Reveal result adds the node, even unconnected, and selects it. A non-match shows 'No matching concept or paragraph.'
steps: type a concept name, §N or N
pick the item from the Result dropdown
press Reveal result
continue with Reveal connected nodes from it
serves_tasks: Find an item by name or number and bring it into view

features.name: Sequential passage reader tied to the graph
features.general: Show the full text of the selected passage with previous/next buttons. Moving to a passage adds it to the network and selects it, so reading in order also grows the network.
features.specific: For a selected paragraph, the panel shows its Latta text (with Theodicy references), '← §N-1' and '§N+1 →' buttons, and the paragraph's linked concepts. Going to an undiscovered paragraph adds it (e.g. §52: 7 → 8 nodes). §1 has no previous button.
steps: select or search a paragraph
read its canonical text
press ← previous or next → to move one paragraph
optionally press Reveal connected nodes to bring in its concepts
serves_tasks: Read the source passage for a selected item and see which concepts it is linked to
Step through passages in order while keeping track of what has been discovered

features.name: Full-network inspection with summary metrics, theme colouring and degree tooltips
features.general: Switch from the partial view to the whole network, with summary cards for node, edge and component counts. Passages stay coloured by category so groupings can be read by eye, and hover tooltips give each node's degree and each edge's relation, so hubs and overall density can be judged.
features.specific: View → Full graph shows Paragraphs 90 / Concepts 64 / Relationships 292 / Components 1 above the full ForceAtlas2-style graph, with paragraph squares coloured by editorial theme. Hovering a node gives name, ID and Degree (God 31); hovering an edge gives 'God — related to — Happiness'. Plot zoom and pan also work here but are incidental.
steps: choose View → Full graph
read the metric cards
look at how theme-coloured paragraph squares group
hover large nodes to read their degree
hover edges to read relationships
switch back to Progressive reader
serves_tasks: View the complete network with its summary counts and see how passages group by theme
Find the most highly connected items and read individual links

features.name: Network colour scheme editor with category colouring and reset
features.general: Set colours for each node type, links, highlighted links and backgrounds, and turn per-category colouring on or off. Category colouring is what lets a reader see thematic groupings in the network; each category has its own colour picker, and one button restores the defaults.
features.specific: Colors & graph display has colour pickers for Concept nodes, Paragraph nodes, Relationships, Selected relationships, Graph background and Dashboard background. Its 'Color paragraphs by theme' checkbox (with one picker per theme) drives the theme reading of the Full graph; Reset appearance restores the defaults.
steps: expand Colors & graph display
toggle Color paragraphs by theme
open a colour picker and choose a colour (or type a hex code)
check the redrawn graph (labels change colour for contrast)
press Reset appearance
serves_tasks: Recolour node types, links and backgrounds, or switch category colouring off, then restore the defaults

screens_never_reached: Node selection by clicking in the graph. The guidance text says 'select a node in the graph', but every click on a node in this headless browser only dimmed all markers (Plotly selection state) and never opened the detail panel. Selection was done through the sidebar list, search and paragraph navigation instead.

Three themes (Natural and Psychic Hierarchy; Bodies, Souls, and Nature; Conclusion) were listed in the Theme dropdown but opened by neither the explorer nor the replay. Truth, Reason, and God was opened only in the replay (check/screens/003.webp).
A paragraph node's hover tooltip with its canonical text. No paragraph node was hovered; only concept nodes and an edge were.
not_done: Graph-click selection could not be used: clicking a node directly in the graph only dimmed the markers and selected nothing (screens/005.webp, screens/014.webp, screens/038.webp). Every goal was still reached through the other selection routes.
Toggling legend entries (e.g. hiding Paragraphs) in the Full graph. The Plotly toolbar sits on top of the legend, and a ref click timed out.
The Plotly Fullscreen, Autoscale and Reset axes buttons and box-zoom mode were not tried individually. Zoom in, wheel zoom, pan and the sidebar Fit to screen button were tested.

Comparing themes structurally beyond their seeds, § ranges and paragraph colour in the Full graph. The app has no per-theme metrics; the Full graph shows only whole-network metrics. Switching theme also discards the current exploration (screens/060.webp), so explorations can't be compared side by side.
The Full graph has no ranked list of 'most connected concepts'. Degree is only shown in hover tooltips and by node size.
The downloaded plot-image.png was not opened (it is a binary image). Only its download was confirmed (screens/067.webp).
